applicability_notes: Single-rate treaty cap with no substantial-holder split. Article 10(2) applies a flat 10% cap on source-state withholding on dividends regardless of beneficial owner type. The literal treaty text is uncharacteristically terse — the verbatim Article 10(2) reads "the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent." (with period; the "of the gross amount of the dividends" base is implicit; cf. Article 12(2) royalties which does spell out "of the gross amount of such royalties"). The treaty has NO most-favoured-nation (MFN) clause (verified absent from the PDF body via search for "most-favoured" / "MFN" / "third State" / "OECD" — none match; also UAE is NOT on the CBDT Circular 3/2022 list of 6 MFN-clause treaties: Netherlands / France / Switzerland / Sweden / Spain / Hungary) so UAE is unaffected by the 2023 Indian Supreme Court Nestlé-case ruling. Article 25 is the Elimination-of-Double-Taxation clause — paragraph 1 is a general savings-clause; paragraph 2 is the Indian-resident credit clause (income tax + capital tax + special surtax sub-clause for corporate Indian residents — natural-person investors fall under the base income-tax sentence); paragraph 3 is the UAE-resident credit clause; paragraph 4 is a UNILATERAL tax-sparing provision explicitly scoped "For the purpose of paragraph (3)" — deeming Indian income-tax-incentive exemptions as if paid for paragraph 3 purposes (applies ONLY to UAE-residents receiving Indian income; NOT to Indian residents receiving UAE income — therefore not relevant to Form 67 vendoring). UAE is a 0%-individual-income-tax jurisdiction; the UAE corporate tax introduced in 2023 (9% on taxable corporate profits above AED 375k) does not withhold on dividends paid to non-residents. Practical FTC for Indian-resident IBKR investors in UAE-listed shares (DFM / ADX) typically yields zero foreign tax to credit; the entry is vendored for tri-state lookup completeness and to capture the rare case where UAE-source income (e.g. interest on Indian-resident-owned UAE bank deposits subject to Indian withholding-equivalent treatment elsewhere) is processed through Form 67.

Claiming the 24(3) tax-sparing benefit above the actual foreign WHT is manual work outside the tool. Israel domestic non-resident WHT on dividends is typically 25%; the DTAA cap of 10% reduces this for Indian portfolio individuals (the Israeli payer applies the treaty rate at source upon presentation of a tax-residency certificate).

Article 25(2) is the avoidance-of-double-taxation clause granting India the right to allow Singapore tax as a deduction (a single paragraph covering both the general individual case and the >= 25% corporate-shareholder underlying-tax-credit case; not split into sub-paragraphs unlike India-US Article 25).
